statement: For REPDF C9, an exhaustive single-byte-substitution search per damaged Flate stream (candidates restricted to bytes before zlib's error point when it errors, as in Barral et al.), accepting candidates that inflate cleanly and pass Adler-32 and then filtering by secondary oracles (exact stock-zlib re-encoding where the producer's encoder is replayable, OBS-0303; decoded length vs /Length1; TrueType table checksums; content-stream tokenisation), restores the original stream uniquely and correctly for at least 90% of the 1442 damaged streams, with no unique-but-wrong corrections.
metric: Per damaged stream: unique-and-correct / ambiguous / none / unique-but-wrong, against the original stream bytes; CPU seconds per stream. Report with and without the secondary oracles, to measure Adler-32-only ambiguity.
baseline: Prefix salvage (decode until error), and the stream-level output of qpdf and mutool on the same files.
data: REPDF C9 files and originals (SRC-0002, commit e547d4d); per-stream ground truth from research/experiments/results/flate_c9_probe.csv (OBS-0300). Or the 1,445 cases rebuilt by research/experiments/pr16/build_cases.py (OBS-1012: probe rev 1 missed 3).
notes: Seeds a W1 spec. Each damaged stream has exactly one changed byte (OBS-0300), so the search is at most 255 x compressed length inflations per stream (median length 9547 bytes). Report Save As (54% replayable) and Print to PDF (almost none replayable) separately: the encoder-replay oracle should make Save As corrections nearly unambiguous. Partly run by PR #16's mzbench (OBS-1006, 1007, 1009, 1010): 218/221 inflate-error streams and 323/343 grammar-flagged streams byte-exact, first-accept false accepts 1/245 and 1/324. Uniqueness over all passing candidates and the secondary oracles are still untested; replay alone is not a uniqueness certificate (OBS-0903, OBS-0904). Its 90% target counts 1,442 streams; the corrected count is 1,445 (OBS-1012).
refute_if: Unique-and-correct below 70% of damaged streams, or at least one unique-but-wrong correction, or median CPU time above 60 s per stream on one core.

statement: Given the position of the damaged byte, Brown-2013-style intra-block resynchronization (skip a small window after the damage, decode from every candidate bit offset until the segmentations converge, carry the unknown history as co-indexed symbols so history-dependent bytes stay 'unknown') recovers verbatim a median of at least 50% of the post-damage decoded bytes of single-block C9 streams, where block-level resync recovers 0%, and emits no byte as known that differs from the original.
metric: Per damaged single-block stream: verbatim post-damage fraction, unknown fraction, count of bytes emitted as known but wrong (must be 0), convergence distance in bytes.
baseline: Prefix salvage; block-level resync (next intact block).
data: The 853 damaged C9 streams that are single-block (OBS-0301), with originals.
notes: Localisation is given (oracle) in this first test; combining it with GAP-150 localisation is a second step. Mark Adler's two-dictionary check (CLM-0337) is a cheap way to verify the 'no known-but-wrong byte' property.
refute_if: Median verbatim post-damage fraction below 20%, or any byte emitted as known that differs from the original.

statement: A per-file toolpath selector trained on fidelity labels (agreement with the known original, not 'opens in a viewer') closes at least half of the gap between the single best toolpath and the per-file oracle (virtual best) on held-out damaged PDFs, and with a reject threshold escalates at most 10% of files while keeping the fabrication rate under the pre-registered ceiling.
metric: Share of the single-best/virtual-best gap closed on the primary endpoint; fabrication rate of auto-accepted files; escalation rate.
baseline: Single best toolpath; the fixed Resave/TemplateAssemble order of the current design.
data: Needs several toolpaths run on a damaged corpus with known originals (REPDF for development only; the held-out suite for the claim).
notes: Answers RQ5 / gentle-gosling s2. Candidate threshold methods: Chow's reject rule (SRC-0331), learning to defer (SRC-0330); candidate escalation design: guided data repair (SRC-0329).
refute_if: Selector closes less than 25% of the single-best/virtual-best gap, or needs to escalate more than 30% of files to meet the fabrication ceiling.

statement: For the 798 Adler-only damaged font streams in REPDF C9 (median compressed length about 16.6 KB, OBS-1003), taking the first TrueType/OpenType table whose checksum fails in the corrupted output as the damage locator, mapping that table's output range back to compressed positions through inflate checkpoints, and searching the 255 alternative byte values only there, restores at least 70% of them byte-exact within 20 s CPU each. An unlocalized full-range search finishes only 59.6-66% of 4-16 KiB streams in 20 s (OBS-1010, CLM-1019) and fewer of the larger ones.
metric: Per Adler-only font stream: byte-exact / accepted-but-wrong / not found / timeout against the original decoded font; localizer hit rate (damaged output position inside the first failing table); searched window in compressed bytes; CPU seconds per stream.
baseline: PR #16's unlocalized checkpointed full-range search (mzbench, OBS-1007 and OBS-1010) with the same 20 s budget, on the same machine.
data: REPDF C9 (SRC-0002, commit e547d4d); damaged-stream cases rebuilt by research/experiments/pr16/build_cases.py from c9exp.py Part A.
notes: PR #16's E6 numbers (all 12,532 tables of intact fonts pass their checksums; the first failing table holds the damage in 765 of 766 damaged fonts, CLM-1026) are claims only: no committed script (CLM-1027, CLM-1067). Rebuild E6 first. A passing set of table checksums is also a secondary acceptance oracle beyond Adler-32 (GAP-052); report its false-accept rate separately. The corrupted font may change length after the damage, so table offsets come from the corrupted output's table directory; damage in the directory itself needs a fallback window.
refute_if: Fewer than 70% of the 798 Adler-only C9 font streams restored byte-exact within 20 s CPU each; or the first failing table misses the damaged output position in more than 5% of damaged fonts; or any accepted candidate that passes Adler-32 and every table checksum differs from the original.

statement: On multi-revision PDFs whose last incremental update is truncated or partly overwritten, resolving duplicate objects and trailers by 'last well-formed copy wins' (a later copy replaces an earlier one only if it parses completely; each generation is a distinct key) recovers the latest complete revision's pages more often than the design's 'last in byte order wins' (§17.2), and never recovers fewer files.
metric: Share of files whose recovered page count and per-page extracted text equal the latest complete revision (ground truth: the undamaged file cut at the last complete update); files won by each rule alone.
baseline: 'Last in byte order wins' as in §17.2 and as qpdf and Ghostscript do (CLM-0501, CLM-0541); pdf.js's parse-gated rule (CLM-0517) as a second comparator.
data: Not yet built: multi-revision PDFs (incremental saves from several producers) truncated at random offsets inside the final update; prevalence of such files is GAP-017.
notes: From PR #16's rank-5 change (CLM-1046, CLM-1073), which is design reasoning, not a measurement. Also log revisions the rule drops, since shadowed revisions are forensic evidence (CLM-1054, GAP-016).
refute_if: On at least 200 truncated multi-revision files, last-well-formed-wins recovers the latest complete revision in no more files than last-in-byte-order-wins, or fails on any file that last-in-byte-order-wins recovers.

statement: Replacing prefix salvage with PR #16's checkpointed search ladder (error-localized search for inflate-error streams, grammar-localized search for flagged content, CMap and text streams, full-range search for streams up to 4 KiB), which restores about 39% of damaged C9 Flate streams byte-exact (OBS-1014), raises REPDF-comparable OCR word recall on the 100 C9 files by at least 5 percentage points over keep-all prefix salvage.
metric: REPDF-comparable OCR word recall on rendered pages per C9 file (5k plan WP-3.5 harness); paired mean difference vs prefix salvage with a 95% bootstrap interval; per-stream byte-exact share reported alongside.
baseline: Keep-all prefix salvage of every damaged stream (decode until zlib stops), and REPDF's published C9 figure (60.11% in Table 2; 58.77/62.70 in Table 5, CLM-1035).
data: REPDF C9 files and originals (SRC-0002, commit e547d4d).
notes: Needs the OCR-recall harness first. Report Save As and Print to PDF separately, and fonts vs content streams, so the gain can be attributed.
refute_if: Paired mean gain in OCR word recall below 2 percentage points (or a 95% interval whose upper bound is below 5) while at least 35% of damaged streams are restored byte-exact.
